title: Living off the fat of the plant: Powdery mildew fungi thrive on host thylakoid lipids
content: “Eat healthy fats!” is a familiar mantra to promote a balanced diet. It highlights the human need for polyunsaturated fatty acids such as omega-3. Biochemically, omega-3 describes a double bond within a fatty acid chain 3 atoms away from the terminal methyl group. A common example of an omega-3 fatty acid is α-linolenic acid, a carboxylic acid with an 18-carbon chain and 3 cis double bonds (18:3). Essential fats such as α-linolenic acid are vital for human metabolism, and we typically obtain these lipids from plant-based foods like nuts, seeds, and oils.
